# 化油器调节方法
化油器通过油门控制发动机转速，实现空气与燃油混合，空燃比可调。正确设置才能发挥吹风机最大输出功率。
化油器设有三处调节装置：
H= 高速油针
L= 低速油针
T= 怠速调节螺钉

# 基础（出厂）设置
吹风机出厂测试时化油器已预设基础参数：
H 油针逆时针旋至限位终点。
L 油针逆时针旋至限位终点。
推荐怠速转速为 3000 转 / 分钟。

# 高速油针 H
1. 按第 13 页启动吹风机，怠速与半油门交替运转 1-2 分钟预热。
2. 发动机全开油门，调节 H 螺钉直至发动机达到最大转速。
3. 将 H 螺钉逆时针旋 1/8 圈（若限位限制则小于 1/8 圈）。

# 低速油针 L
1. 检查吹风管（15）与喷口（14）已安装到位。
2. 将 H、L 调节螺钉逆时针旋至限位终点。
3. 按第 13 页启动吹风机发动机，怠速与半油门交替运转 1-2 分钟预热。若发动机无法怠速运转，顺时针旋动 T 螺钉直至正常怠速。
4. 调节 T 螺钉，使发动机精准维持怠速，转速不偏高。
5. 微调 L 螺钉，使发动机达到最大怠速转速，然后将 L 螺钉逆时针旋出最多 1/4 圈。
6. 必要时旋动 T 螺钉提升发动机转速。
注意！调节 H 油针时，全油门持续时间最长 10 秒，之后需怠速运转至少 10 秒。, ["Manual04_17", "Manual04_42"]

---

- **灵活调整**：在运动过程中，你可以随时切换到其他程序，比如暂停当前运动、切换到心率控制模式等。

---

# 如何使用本练习指南 以下是各类速度的说明：
“拖曳速度”为最低操控速度，几乎不加油门。艇体沉入水中，无尾流。   <PIC>   
“半滑航速度”为中等速度，艇首略微抬离水面，但仍在水中行驶，产生尾流。   <PIC>   
“滑航速度”为较快速度，艇体更平稳，在水面滑行，产生尾流。   <PIC>

技巧和应用差异：
1. 拖曳速度：仅产生最小推力，适合低速操控，如靠岸、停靠码头或接近物体（文献6、11）。
2. 半滑航速度：中等速度，适合练习转向和基本操控（文献2、13）。
3. 滑航速度：较快速度，适合快速转向和钓鱼（文献5、9、14）。

# 技能： 深水登艇与静止平衡。

将摩托艇放入水中，在无杂草或杂物、水深至少60厘米（2英尺）的水域中练习，站立在艇旁操作。 切勿在水深不足60厘米（2英尺）的水域操作，否则石子或沙子可能被吸入喷射口，导致叶轮损坏或发动机过热。

训练3：操作姿势 将摩托艇停在陆地，发动机关闭状态下登艇，熟悉《用户/操作手册》中描述的正确操作姿势。然后双眼直视前方，找到每个操控装置并确认使用方法。重复训练直至熟练掌握操控装置。

操作方法： 先在近岸练习，再前往开阔水域。 驾驶者体重越大，平衡艇体难度越高。  练习时不启动发动机。 将熄火绳系在手腕上，在水深至少齐胸的水域让艇漂浮。

滑航速度下，艇体在给定速度下的转向角度有限。车把转向过度时，艇体可能开始侧滑，无法更急转弯。这是因为侧滑时进入喷射口的水量减少，喷嘴排水量下降，转向推力降低。结果是艇体减速，转向更平缓。将车把转回较小角度可恢复正常转向。

---

### **1. 查找滑动搁架**
- 烤箱内部通常有 **上下两层滑动搁架**，位于烤箱两侧或后方轨道上。
- 搁架一般由 **烤盘 + 滑动支架** 组成，支架可沿轨道滑动。

---

### **2. 调整搁架位置**
- **向上滑动**：靠近热风出口（烤箱顶部），适合烤制表面需要焦化或上色的食物（如披萨、烤肉）。
- **向下滑动**：靠近烤箱底部，适合烤制底部需要受热的食物（如蛋糕、面包）。
- **中间位置**：适合均匀加热或分层放置食物。

---

### **3. 使用技巧**
- **多层烘烤**：如果烤箱支持多层放置，确保每层搁架之间留有 **足够间距**（避免受热不均或烤盘接触）。
- **热风烤箱**：建议将搁架放置在 **烤箱中央**，让热风循环更均匀。
- **特殊需求**：
  - 烤蛋糕：上层搁架略低，防止顶部过干。
  - 烤肉类：上层搁架略高，锁住肉汁。
  - 烘烤饼干：搁架靠近顶部，使表面焦化。

- **避免超载**：不要在单个烤盘上放置过多食物，以免变形或烤焦。

[User Question]
What is the purpose of the EMERG PARALLEL switch on the battery switch assembly? How does it affect the charging of the batteries during normal operation?

[Assistant Response]
The EMERG PARALLEL switch on the battery switch assembly is designed to handle situations where the start battery is discharged and cannot be used to start the engine. When this switch is turned to the ON position; it connects the two batteries in parallel; allowing the house battery to provide power for starting the engine. This is an emergency measure to ensure the engine can be started even if the start battery is dead.

During normal operation; the EMERG PARALLEL switch should remain in the OFF position. In this position; the batteries are not connected in parallel; and the system operates with the batteries in series; allowing both batteries to be charged automatically while the engine is running. Keeping it in the OFF position ensures that the batteries are charged separately and that the emergency parallel connection is not activated unnecessarily.

Its important to note that after using the emergency parallel function to start the engine; the switch should be turned back to the OFF position once the engine is running or charged to prevent any unintended parallel operation; which could lead to unequal charging or potential damage to the batteries., ["Manual09_45", "Manual09_42", "Manual09_43", "Manual09_44", "Manual09_100", "Manual09_101", "Manual09_262", "Manual20_48"]

Operation of the watercraft must be in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the waterway on which it is used. These rules are used internationally; and are also enforced by the United States Coast Guard and local agencies. You should be aware of these rules; and follow them whenever you encounter another vessel on the water. Several sets of rules prevail according to geographic location; but are all basically the same as the International Rules of the Road. The rules presented here in this Owner’s/Operator’s Manual are condensed; and have been provided for your convenience only. Consult your local U.S. Coast Guard Auxiliary or Department of Motor Vehicles for a complete set of rules governing the waters in which you will be operating your watercraft.

<PIC>

There are three main situations that you may encounter with other vessels which could lead to a collision unless the Steering Rules are followed: Meeting: you are approaching another vessel head-on. Crossing: you are traveling across another vessel’s path. Overtaking: you are passing or being passed by another vessel.

Whenever two vessels on the water meet one another; one vessel has the right-of-way; it is called the “stand-on” vessel. The vessel that does not have the right-of-way is called the “give-way” or “burdened” vessel. These rules determine which vessel has the right-of-way; and what each vessel should do.

The vessel with the right-of-way has the duty to continue its course and speed; except to avoid an immediate collision. When you maintain your direction and speed; the other vessel will be able to determine how best to avoid you.

The vessel which does not have the right-of-way has the duty to take positive and timely action to stay out of the way of the stand-on vessel. Normally; you should not cross in front of the vessel with the right-of-way. You should slow down or change directions briefly and pass behind the other vessel. You should always move in such a way that the operator of the other vessel can see what you are doing. The General Prudential Rule regarding the right-of-way is that if a collision appears unavoidable; neither boat has the rightsuccessfully way. Both boats must avoid the collision. In other words; follow the standard rules except when a collision will occur unless both vessels try to avoid each other. If that is the case; both vessels become give-away vessels., ["Manual09_28"]

# RIDING UPHILL  
You should practice first on gentle slopes. Try more difficult climbs only after you have developed your skill. As you approach a hill; accelerate before you start the climb; and then reduce the throttle opening to prevent track slippage. It is also important to keep your weight on the uphill side at all times. On climbs straight up the hill; this can be accomplished by leaning forward; and on steeper inclines; stand on the running boards and lean forward over the handlebars. (Also see “CROSSING A SLOPE.”)  
Slow down as you reach the crest of the hill; and be prepared to react to obstacles; sharp drops; or other people or vehicles which may be on the other side.  
If you are unable to continue up a hill; do not spin the track. Stop the engine and set the parking brake. Then pull the rear of the snowmobile around to point the machine back down the hill. Do not get on the downhill side of the machine. When the snowmobile is pointed downhill; restart the engine; release the parking brake; and descend the hill.  
<PIC>, ["Manual34_129"]

When riding downhill;keep speed to a minimum.
It is important to apply just enough throttle to keep the clutch engaged while descending the hill.
This will allow you to use engine compression to help slow the machine; and to keep the snowmobile from rolling freely down the hill.
Also apply the brake frequently;withlight pressure. <PIC>, ["Manual34_128"]
